messages.subject: [geomorph-r-package] CI through bootstrapping for modularity.test
parts:
Hi there, 

Could you explain the bootstrapping procedure for calculating confidence intervals (CI) in the "modularity.test" function using "boot.CR"? I could not understand what "boot.CR" does in https://rdrr.io/cran/geomorph/src/R/geomorph.support.code.r. As I understand, bootstrapping involves resampling specimens with replacement from each group, equal to the original sample size of that group. Is it the same procedure used for calculating CI in the "modularity.test" function?

According to the geomorph document, statistical significance is evaluated by randomly assigning measurements into pre-assigned partitions by a certain number of permutations. So, it is different from calculating CI using bootstrapping, correct? For example, even if the upper tail of the 95% CI is below 1.0, it is not related to statistical significance of the CR value as the p-value is not evaluated by CI through the bootstrapping procedure, right? Please correct me if I am wrong.

Thank you and have a great day!

Best regards,
Hyunwoo

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] CI through bootstrapping for modularity.test
parts:
Hyunwoo,

 

Yes to your first question. The Bootstrapping for CR obtains bootstrap samples of individuals (i.e., samping with replacement). Each time that sample is used to calculate the CR, based on the pre-defined modules. From these 95% CI are obtained around the observed CR value to provide one a measure of uncertainty (a standard use of the bootstrap).

 

To your second question: the bootstrap CI have nothing to do with the significance test of modularity. The latter is evaluated via permutation of variables (see the original 2016 paper and the help file).

 

Dean
